Usefulness of running in local politics?

You're thinking a little small in my opinion. It's not just about effecting local change, running in small elections affects national change. The reason being is that by running in local elections you spend a lot of time meeting people. This in turn makes people aware of the policies of the Libertarian Party. In turn when they see a national candidate, they don't automatically ignore them but remember the local candidate that ran under that party and associate the national candidate with those same principles.

I think that it is good to affect local change, I just think that getting the word out about the LP is more than just about local change. It creates a ripple that can become a wave.

I've always said if the LP really wants to make a huge impact they need to get more local candidates elected. I'm not saying don't run presidential candidates because it still spreads our message to people but local is where its at. If we could get LP candidates elected to state houses and senates or even as a governor, we could have a better chance of winning.

Just a heads up if you decide to do this, some legal requirements and ordinances enacted by municipalities are due to mandates from the State and Federal government.

Also, I would attend and observe several council meetings and if possible sub committee meetings to get a flavor for the process and the players. Talk to people on the council about your beliefs and get to know them a bit. Otherwise even if you do end up winning a council seat, you might be persona non grata and have zero influence.

I have had discussions with various local politicians over the years, representing the spectrum of political thought, including a mayor who I think had libertarian leanings (it's been a few years). My overall impression is they are generally knowledgeable and we'll spoken. I say go for it, but don't underestimate your fellow council members.
